findings.current: Summary and applicability treat AIS-038 Rev.2 and AIS-156 as one set for M/N passenger-car/light-truck EV programs; source_url is the AIS-156 PDF
findings.proposed: AIS-038 Rev.2 = electric power train + REESS safety for M and N categories (UN R100 counterpart). AIS-156 = L-category (2W/3W/quadricycle) power train + REESS, so it is not applicable to passenger cars (M1) or light trucks (N1); point source_url to AIS-038 Rev.2 and list AIS-156 only for L-category (UN R136 counterpart)
findings.evidence: Search result: "AIS-156 prescribes safety requirements with respect to the electric power train and REESS of L category vehicles"; "AIS-038 Rev.2 Part I covers ... motor vehicles of categories M and N". Record body: "AIS-156 should be applicability-filtered because it can be category-specific".

findings.current: un_equivalent: UN R157; un_equivalent_ai: UN R155, UN R156
findings.proposed: Remove R157 as an equivalent (R157 is ALKS, a regulation not a functional-safety process standard). ISO 26262 has no single UN counterpart; at most reference it as supporting evidence for R79/R13-H/R157 safety cases (R155 cyber, R156 SUMS are not counterparts)
findings.evidence: Repo body: "Not generally a direct government regulation ... not a substitute for each government regulation"; UN R157 covers Automated Lane Keeping Systems, ISO 26262 is a functional-safety standard (standard knowledge).

findings.proposed: No direct UN equivalent. R157 (ALKS) is a legal regulation; ISO 21448 SOTIF is a voluntary engineering standard that may support ADAS approvals (e.g. R157, R79, R171). Remove R155 (cybersecurity) entirely
findings.evidence: Repo body: "Not a direct government regulation"; R155 is cybersecurity, unrelated to SOTIF.
